Same-run production universal leaf updates at 4,000 unrelated siblings versus none. The fixed scoped path measures near 1x; 8x leaves sub-millisecond timer/JIT headroom while rejecting both the former whole-root replay (hundreds of times slower) and the object-driver full-map clone (tens of times slower).

State in the root component replays from the root range, and every clean leaf subtree is adopted without re-rendering (issue #574 follow-up). The dirty twin rewrites all 4,000 leaf props per press, so it must re-render each leaf; the clean run measures well under half of that (~0.25x observed). A ratio near 1x means retained-subtree adoption stopped engaging and clean leaves are re-rendering again.

One keyed @for item's setState hoists to its 20-item list component instead of replaying the root, so 4,000 out-of-scope siblings must not change its cost. Rejects the anonymous-owner bail that sent list-item state through a whole-root replay.

A leaf setState under an idle @try boundary stays scoped; only an active suspense or error episode may fall back to the root. Rejects the blanket ancestor-boundary bail that disabled scoped updates for any app with an error boundary near the root.

A leaf update that inserts or removes one host commits through the scope's physical frame (nearest host parent plus end anchor) instead of replaying the root. Rejects the shape-stability bail that sent every structural update through a whole-root replay.

Compact leaf rows driven by their list component's selection state replay only that component (its 100 rows), so unrelated siblings must not change the cost. Rejects the compact-range bail that forced list selection through a whole-root replay.

Eight times as many retained fallback collapsed-template event sites should take no more than 1.5 times linear growth. The optimized node-local cursor measures about 7-8x; the former whole-template search measures about 26x on the same fixture.

An inline getter changes what is read, not subscription ownership: each mounted universal reader needs one lifetime release.
